# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 72 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 72 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_072_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 8, Part 3 — More Rod Categories

**72:1** "Those who surrendered their rods more dry than green — these are those who believed yet lived a divided life: they did some good but also committed much evil. Some of them repented and were placed in the first tower; others repented and were placed in the second tower; still others did not repent at all. These remain even now among the unrepentant."

**72:2** "Those who surrendered their rods more green than dry — these are those who for the most part led a good life but committed some evil, and who had not long been among the faithful. They repented quickly when they heard my commandments. Their dwelling is in the first tower."

**72:3** "Those who surrendered their rods green but with dried tips — these are those who were at all times good and faithful, yet who had some measure of envy and strife toward one another over matters of rank and dignity. When they heard my words, the greater part of them repented quickly, and their dwelling is in the first tower. Some were double-minded, and their dwelling is in the second tower."

**72:4** "Those who surrendered their rods half-green and half-dry — these are those who had become deeply involved in business dealings and had not kept close to the holy ones. For this reason, half of them is living and half is dead. Many of them, when they heard my commandments, repented; and those who repented dwell in the first tower. Some were altogether double-minded and fell away entirely. These have lost their lives."

**72:5** "Those who surrendered their rods entirely green, with shoots and fruit — these are those who suffered hardship for the sake of the name and endured with a whole heart, and who laid down their very lives."

---

*LOGOS renders according to the Greek text of P.Mich. 130 with attention to the formal typological structure and pastoral theology of Similitude 8.*
